title: Adaptive Ops Slate for Batching Inspector — compact configurator and one-click dry-run
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a compact, action-oriented side panel (the 'Ops Slate') inside the Redwood Console Batching Inspector that surfaces recommendation snippets, explainers, and safety guardrails for cache+batch policies. The slate is designed for operators and platform engineers who need a lightweight, reversible way to preview and apply batching/cache changes with an emphasis on clarity about cost/latency trade-offs and rollback safety. This ticket covers the design exploration, annotated prototype, copy guidelines, and acceptance criteria for handoff to frontend engineering.
background: We have several large, dense recommendation surfaces in the console that are great for discovery but noisy for quick ops changes. Support and platform teams asked for a compact, opinionated flow that minimizes context switching: 1) summarize recommended change, 2) show measurable impact (tokens/sec, est $/k tokens, latency P95), 3) highlight risk and fallback paths, and 4) allow a dry-run or canary rollout. The Ops Slate is the lightweight UX layer to achieve this.
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want a concise summary of a batching recommendation so I can evaluate and act quickly without navigating multiple dashboards.
As an SRE, I want a dry-run simulation that shows estimated latency and cost delta so I can validate impact before applying changes to production.
As a product manager, I want a clear record of who applied a policy and what fallback was configured so audits and regressions are easier to investigate.
proposed_solution: Introduce a right-rail 'Ops Slate' that attaches to the Batching Inspector page. Main components: 1) Header with short recommendation title + risk badge (low/medium/high). 2) Impact strip with three micro-metrics (cost delta, P95 latency delta, throughput delta) with sparkline miniature. 3) Compact explainer paragraph (single sentence) + 'Why this change' collapsible. 4) Guardrail checklist (auto-validated toggles): prefix-protection, max-token-window, KV-cache affinity. 5) Two primary actions: 'Dry-run (simulate)' and 'Apply (canary)'. 6) Advanced link to open the full Batch/Cache Configurator for deep edits. The slate should be keyboard accessible, mobile-responsive inside console panels, and have progressive disclosure so novice users see only the headline and actions while expert users can expand details.
acceptance_criteria: Ops Slate prototype exists in Figma with annotated interactions for header, impact strip, explainer, guardrails, and primary actions.
Prototype includes a simulated dry-run flow that updates micro-metrics and shows a green/yellow/red risk indication based on constraints.
Copy drafts for risk badges, guardrail descriptions, and CTA microcopy reviewed and approved by content design.
Design tokens and spacing documented for frontend: width constraints (320px min, 480px max), typography scales, and iconography.
Accessibility checklist completed: ARIA for toggles, contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical text, keyboard focus order defined.
Handoff notes created with engineering tickets for integration and telemetry requirements.
decisions: Show only three micro-metrics in the impact strip to reduce cognitive load (cost, latency P95, throughput).
Dry-run will run a client-side simulation based on historical trace slices and not mutate production config unless 'Apply' is confirmed.
Canary rollout UI will default to 5% traffic unless operator explicitly adjusts, to reduce blast radius.
Guardrails will be pre-checked based on the target route's historical safety signals; operators can uncheck but will see a required justification modal if unchecking increases risk.
tradeoffs: Keeping slate compact means fewer inline knobs — advanced edits funnel users to the full configurator which could add friction for power users.
Client-side dry-run yields faster feedback but can diverge from server-side outcomes for very recent model/kernel changes; we annotate this risk in the UI.
Defaulting canary to 5% minimizes risk but may delay detection of regressions for low-frequency routes.
implementation_notes: Frontend: implement right-rail responsive panel with slide-in animation and ARIA region labeling. (ENG-21398)
Backend: expose a dry-run simulation endpoint that accepts route history window and returns estimated deltas. (ENG-21402)
Telemetry: emit events for slate_open, dryrun_request, dryrun_result, apply_start, apply_complete with cost_estimate and risk_score fields.
Rollouts: integrate with rollout service so 'Apply (canary)' triggers a controlled rollout and creates an audit entry in Audit Log 2.0.
